tools.name: list_open_design_skills
tools.description: Lists available Open Design skills, design templates, and remixable examples — reusable design-task recipes, rendering styles, and (for 'example' entries) actual starting artifacts bundled with this server. Each result's id is namespaced as 'od:<mode>:<name>' (e.g. 'od:deck:guizang-ppt') — pass this full id as skillId to prepare_open_design_brief or remix_open_design_example. Each result's 'source' field is 'skill', 'design-template', or 'example'. Some results include an 'examplePrompt' — prefer it (or lightly adapt it) over inventing your own brief when it closely fits. A result with remixable: true has an actual rendered starting artifact, bundled inside this server and never a file you can find on disk — prefer remix_open_design_example (which copies it into the workspace for you) over prepare_open_design_brief for those. Optionally filter by a free-text query, an exact mode, an exact source, and/or remixableOnly to see only entries with a rendered starting artifact. SURFACES: when the user names a kind of thing to make — a prototype or landing page, mobile app, slides, document, wireframe, animation, résumé, research synthesis, data report, poster or flier, social post, diagram — call this tool with surface set to that surface's id first (call with surface "list" to see the ids) and pick from its entries; if the surface names a prompt, follow that flow. STUBS: an entry with stub: true only advertises an upstream skill and has no instructions here — never pick one; choose a non-stub entry instead. PAGING: with more than 40 matches the result is { total, offset, nextOffset, modes, note, entries }, 100 compact entries (id, name, one-line summary, mode, source) per page; narrow with mode, source, query or surface for the full entries, or pass nextOffset as offset for the next page. If a query returns few or no results, call this tool again with a broader query or no arguments at all to browse the full catalog — do NOT search the filesystem, grep, or read any file (this catalog is not stored anywhere as a single readable file such as a content.json, index, or schema file; it exists only inside this server's own runtime and is reachable exclusively through this tool).

query.description: Optional free-text filter, matched against skill name, description, and triggers.

surface.description: A kind of thing to make — returns that surface's entries in curated order (the recipe first, then its remixable example; never catalog stubs), plus the surface's own prompt and clarifying questions. Pass "list" to get the surfaces themselves (id, label, description, entryCount) and the goals (plain-language aims such as "Promote an event", each with the surfaces it leads to). Ignores the other filters.

goal.description: A goal id from the "list" result (e.g. "promote-event", "get-hired"): returns the surfaces that goal leads to, in order, the first marked default. Use it when the user said what the design is for but not what kind of thing to make.

remixableOnly.description: Optional: when true, only return entries with remixable: true (an actual rendered starting artifact to remix).

offset.description: Optional: where a paged listing starts. Pass the previous result's nextOffset for the next page.

tools.name: list_open_design_design_systems
tools.description: Lists available Open Design design systems — brand-inspired visual token sets (palette, typography, spacing, component rules), each with a 'category' and an 'active' flag marking the current active design system, if any. Optionally filter by a free-text query and/or an exact category. MOBILE: category 'Mobile Apps' holds systems adapted from real iOS apps (ids ending in '-ios', e.g. 'spotify-ios'). For phone screens prefer them, even over a same-brand web system ('spotify'), which stays the one for web pages. If a query returns few or no results, call this tool again with a broader query or no arguments at all to browse the full catalog — do NOT search the filesystem, grep, or read any file (this catalog is not stored anywhere as a single readable file such as a content.json, index, or schema file; it exists only inside this server's own runtime and is reachable exclusively through this tool).

query.description: Optional free-text filter, matched against design system name, summary, and category.

tools.name: recommend_open_design_design_systems
tools.description: Recommends 3 to 5 Open Design design systems for a design, ranked the same way every time, each with a one-line reason and its look (light or dark, accent, display type, corner shape). Use it before prepare_open_design_brief when the user hasn't named a design system or a look, no design system is active, and they want a new design (not an edit, remix or export). Fill the profile from the request, the conversation and the workspace; leave out what you don't know. If the result includes `questions`, ask them once, in one message, and accept "you pick" (then use the first recommendation). Otherwise use the first recommendation, say which one you used and that they can switch. Does NOT change the active design system: pass the chosen id to prepare_open_design_brief. Product-named looks (Stripe, Linear…) are recommended only when the user names that product, via likeBrands or the brief.

moods.description: How it should feel, most important first.

theme.description: Light or dark, only if the user said or the context makes it clear.

likeBrands.description: Products or sites the user wants it to feel like, e.g. ['Notion'].

avoid.description: Design system ids or moods to leave out.

brief.description: The request in the user's words.

like.description: Rank by how close each system's tokens are in style to this one: a design system id, or the bundleDir an extraction returned. Use it for "something like X but brand-free"; the named system itself is left out.

tools.name: scan_open_design_app
tools.description: Reads the app in this workspace (never changes a file) and reports what a design for it should reuse: framework and styling, its tokens with the file and line each comes from (Tailwind theme, CSS variables including dark and [data-theme] blocks, MUI theme), its light and dark themes, its exported components with their variant props (most imported first), and its screens (Next.js, Expo Router and React Router routes). Use it before designing a screen, flow or redesign for an app that already exists, then show the user what was found. With name (after the user agrees), it also returns a DESIGN.md, tokens.css and components.json to save as a design system, so briefs list the app's components and the check flags hard-coded and undefined tokens. When a design system was already saved from the same app, it reports what changed since. Bounded to 2,000 files and 1 MB; never reads .env files.

root.description: Workspace-relative folder of the app, for a monorepo (default the workspace root).

name.description: A name for the design system to save from the app, e.g. "Acme app". Only after the user agrees to save one.

tools.name: read_open_design_source
tools.description: Converts a workspace document (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, PDF, Markdown, text or CSV) into Markdown under the output directory's sources/ folder, extracts its embedded images, and returns an outline (headings with line ranges and sizes), never the full text. Read the returned markdownPath yourself, by line range, for the sections you need. Cached by content hash. Use it to look into a source before deciding how to use it; prepare_open_design_brief with `sources` calls it for you. PDFs need `pdftotext` (poppler); without it the result says to read the PDF with your own tools.

Returns an 'instructions' string you must follow, plus a 'suggestedEntryPath'. brief.description: The user's design brief / request, in their own words.

collectionId.description: Set this (a slug you derive once from the collection name, reused verbatim on every call) when this artifact is one screen of a multi-screen design collection — see the "design collections" guidance for the full workflow.

collectionName.description: A short display name for the collection, e.g. "Fintech Onboarding Flow". Required together with collectionId.

screenRole.description: Required together with collectionId â this screen's short role label, e.g. "splash", "value-prop", "checkout".

Reads the content inventory that extract_open_design_design_system wrote with content: true (call that first) and the audit_open_design_site findings if the site was audited, and adds a section binding the site's own words, listing the problems to fix and, unless owned is true, the concept ribbon. owned.description: True only when the user says the site is theirs or the work is commissioned: no concept ribbon.

Adds a Canvas section with the exact size, units, safe area and, for print, bleed and minimum type size, so any skill can produce a post or poster at that size. Screen: x-image (1600×900), ig-square (1080×1080 per card), ig-portrait (1080×1350), pinterest-pin (1000×1500, 20 MB), story (1080×1920), xhs-card (1080×1440 per card), yt-thumbnail (1280×720), linkedin-image (1200×627), og-image (1200×630), x-header (1500×500), linkedin-banner (1584×396), email-header (600×200, captured at 2×), and display ads banner-mrec (300×250), banner-leaderboard (728×90), banner-skyscraper (160×600), banner-mobile (320×50), and shop images shop-product (2048×2048), shop-banner (1920×800), shop-collection (1920×600). Print (trim sizes, authored in mm with bleed): a4, a3, a2, a1, a0, a5, a6, a7, letter, tabloid, poster-18x24, poster-24x36, postcard-4x6, business-card, business-card-us, and cards with rounded corners trading-card, tarot-card, mini-card. tools.name: prepare_open_design_exploration
tools.description: Use INSTEAD of prepare_open_design_brief when the user explicitly asks for options, directions, alternatives or several versions of a design. Assigns 2–4 deliberately different directions (visual styles when no design system is active, layout/narrative structures when one is, or labels you pass for a named axis), writes the exploration's plan, and returns sharedInstructions plus one short instructions block, entry path and directionId per direction. Directions are quick sketches; only the one the user picks is built out. Writes no design files: write each direction yourself (follow sharedInstructions + that direction's instructions), register it with explorationId and directionId, then call compare_open_design_exploration. STYLE TILES: with skillId od:design-system:style-tile the directions are compact color + type tiles (default 4, visual axis even with an active design system; axis "custom" with an active system evolves it). Choosing one with next "save-design-system" copies the tile's tokens verbatim.

skillId.description: A skill id from list_open_design_skills, in its full 'od:<mode>:<name>' form.

brief.description: The user's design brief / request, in their own words.

count.description: How many directions: 2–4, default 3; for the style-tile skill 2–6, default 4.

axis.description: What the directions differ in. Omit for the default: 'structure' when a design system is active (brand stays fixed), otherwise 'visual'. 'visual' with an active design system sets that system aside for this exploration. 'custom' needs customDirections.

directionIds.description: Optional: pick specific directions instead of the default order. Visual ids: modern-minimal, human-approachable, tech-utility, editorial-monocle (editorial/publishing briefs), brutalist-experimental (art, agency, manifesto). Structure ids for pages: classic-hero-grid, story-led-scroll, product-ui-first, dense-utility; for decks: problem-solution, narrative-journey, data-led, demo-first.

designSystemId.description: Optional design system id. If omitted, the active one is used. If given, it also becomes the active one.

tools.name: create_open_design_design_system
tools.description: Composes instructions for authoring a brand-new, custom design system as a DESIGN.md file plus a sibling tokens.css following the Open Design token contract. notMade.description: Outputs the job asks for that this run did not make.

notes.description: A sentence or two for the run record and summary: choices made without the person, anything odd.

tools.name: set_open_design_workspace
tools.description: Sets the folder Open Design works in for the rest of this session: where designs, manifests and .open-design/config.json are written, and what every workspace-relative path in other tools' results is relative to. Call it once, before any other Open Design tool, when this server can't know the user's folder on its own — in Claude Desktop chats with a connected folder it starts in the user's home folder. Pass the folder's absolute path on the machine this server runs on (in Claude Desktop, the path get_device_info lists under connectedFolders), not the path your own file tools see it under. Afterwards, join the workspace-relative paths other tools return onto your own path for that folder when you read or write files. Not needed in Claude Code, Codex or VS Code, which start the server in the project.

path.description: Absolute path of the user's folder on the machine this server runs on.

tools.poisoning_detail: Tool description is 809 characters. Long descriptions can hide malicious instructions.

tools.name: use_open_design_managed_workspace
tools.description: For a Claude Desktop chat with NO connected folder only, where your own file tools (if any) can't reach this server's files: creates, or reopens, a folder this server keeps for the design (under ~/Open Design/ unless configured otherwise) and makes it the workspace for the rest of the session. Call it once, before other Open Design tools, then save every design file with write_open_design_file instead of your own file tools. Tell the user the folder's absolute path from the result, so they can open it. Pass the same name in a later chat to continue the same design. If the chat has a connected folder, call set_open_design_workspace instead.

name.description: A short name for the design or project, e.g. "Coffee poster". The folder is named after it.

tools.poisoning_detail: Tool description is 647 characters. Long descriptions can hide malicious instructions.

tools.name: write_open_design_file
tools.description: Saves one design file you wrote into the folder use_open_design_managed_workspace opened, exactly as given, and returns its path, size and SHA-256. Only works in that folder: anywhere else, write files with your own file-editing tools. Pass the whole file each time (to edit, send the full new version). path is workspace-relative and must be under the output directory, e.g. ".open-design/coffee-poster/coffee-poster.html". Allowed: .html .htm .css .js .mjs .json .svg .md .txt .csv as text, and .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif .woff .woff2 as base64 with encoding "base64"; at most 5 MiB. Manifests, comments, config.json, exports/ and check screenshots belong to other tools and are refused. Never deletes or moves anything. After writing an entry file, call register_open_design_artifact as usual.

path.description: Workspace-relative path under the output directory, e.g. ".open-design/coffee-poster/coffee-poster.html".

content.description: The whole file: text, or base64 for images and fonts.

encoding.description: Set to "base64" for images and fonts. Leave out for text.

tools.poisoning_detail: Steering language in tool description (imperative guidance aimed at the model). Matched pattern in tool 'write_open_design_file': 'Never'

tools.name: probe_show_view
tools.description: Shows the Open Design MCP Apps probe view. Call it once when the user asks to run the probe.

tools.name: probe_payload

tools.name: probe_report
tools.description: Called by the probe view only. Records what the view found.

tools.name: list_open_design_skills
tools.description: Lists available Open Design skills, design templates, and remixable examples — reusable design-task recipes, rendering styles, and (for 'example' entries) actual starting artifacts bundled with this server. Each result's id is namespaced as 'od:<mode>:<name>' (e.g. 'od:deck:guizang-ppt') — pass this full id as skillId to prepare_open_design_brief or remix_open_design_example. Each result's 'source' field is 'skill', 'design-template', or 'example'. Some results include an 'examplePrompt' — prefer it (or lightly adapt it) over inventing your own brief when it closely fits. A result with remixable: true has an actual rendered starting artifact, bundled inside this server and never a file you can find on disk — prefer remix_open_design_example (which copies it into the workspace for you) over prepare_open_design_brief for those. Optionally filter by a free-text query, an exact mode, an exact source, and/or remixableOnly to see only entries with a rendered starting artifact. SURFACES: when the user names a kind of thing to make — a prototype or landing page, mobile app, slides, document, wireframe, animation, résumé, research synthesis, data report, poster or flier, social post, diagram — call this tool with surface set to that surface's id first (call with surface "list" to see the ids) and pick from its entries; if the surface names a prompt, follow that flow. STUBS: an entry with stub: true only advertises an upstream skill and has no instructions here — never pick one; choose a non-stub entry instead. PAGING: with more than 40 matches the result is { total, offset, nextOffset, modes, note, entries }, 100 compact entries (id, name, one-line summary, mode, source) per page; narrow with mode, source, query or surface for the full entries, or pass nextOffset as offset for the next page. If a query returns few or no results, call this tool again with a broader query or no arguments at all to browse the full catalog — do NOT search the filesystem, grep, or read any file (this catalog is not stored anywhere as a single readable file such as a content.json, index, or schema file; it exists only inside this server's own runtime and is reachable exclusively through this tool).

query.description: Optional free-text filter, matched against skill name, description, and triggers.

surface.description: A kind of thing to make — returns that surface's entries in curated order (the recipe first, then its remixable example; never catalog stubs), plus the surface's own prompt and clarifying questions. Pass "list" to get the surfaces themselves (id, label, description, entryCount) and the goals (plain-language aims such as "Promote an event", each with the surfaces it leads to). Ignores the other filters.

goal.description: A goal id from the "list" result (e.g. "promote-event", "get-hired"): returns the surfaces that goal leads to, in order, the first marked default. Use it when the user said what the design is for but not what kind of thing to make.

remixableOnly.description: Optional: when true, only return entries with remixable: true (an actual rendered starting artifact to remix).

offset.description: Optional: where a paged listing starts. Pass the previous result's nextOffset for the next page.

tools.name: list_open_design_design_systems
tools.description: Lists available Open Design design systems — brand-inspired visual token sets (palette, typography, spacing, component rules), each with a 'category' and an 'active' flag marking the current active design system, if any. Optionally filter by a free-text query and/or an exact category. MOBILE: category 'Mobile Apps' holds systems adapted from real iOS apps (ids ending in '-ios', e.g. 'spotify-ios'). For phone screens prefer them, even over a same-brand web system ('spotify'), which stays the one for web pages. If a query returns few or no results, call this tool again with a broader query or no arguments at all to browse the full catalog — do NOT search the filesystem, grep, or read any file (this catalog is not stored anywhere as a single readable file such as a content.json, index, or schema file; it exists only inside this server's own runtime and is reachable exclusively through this tool).

query.description: Optional free-text filter, matched against design system name, summary, and category.

category.description: Optional exact category filter, e.g. 'E-Commerce & Retail'.

tools.name: recommend_open_design_design_systems
tools.description: Recommends 3 to 5 Open Design design systems for a design, ranked the same way every time, each with a one-line reason and its look (light or dark, accent, display type, corner shape). Use it before prepare_open_design_brief when the user hasn't named a design system or a look, no design system is active, and they want a new design (not an edit, remix or export). Fill the profile from the request, the conversation and the workspace; leave out what you don't know. If the result includes `questions`, ask them once, in one message, and accept "you pick" (then use the first recommendation). Otherwise use the first recommendation, say which one you used and that they can switch. Does NOT change the active design system: pass the chosen id to prepare_open_design_brief. Product-named looks (Stripe, Linear…) are recommended only when the user names that product, via likeBrands or the brief.

moods.description: How it should feel, most important first.

theme.description: Light or dark, only if the user said or the context makes it clear.

likeBrands.description: Products or sites the user wants it to feel like, e.g. ['Notion'].

avoid.description: Design system ids or moods to leave out.

brief.description: The request in the user's words.

like.description: Rank by how close each system's tokens are in style to this one: a design system id, or the bundleDir an extraction returned. Use it for "something like X but brand-free"; the named system itself is left out.

tools.name: scan_open_design_app
tools.description: Reads the app in this workspace (never changes a file) and reports what a design for it should reuse: framework and styling, its tokens with the file and line each comes from (Tailwind theme, CSS variables including dark and [data-theme] blocks, MUI theme), its light and dark themes, its exported components with their variant props (most imported first), and its screens (Next.js, Expo Router and React Router routes). Use it before designing a screen, flow or redesign for an app that already exists, then show the user what was found. With name (after the user agrees), it also returns a DESIGN.md, tokens.css and components.json to save as a design system, so briefs list the app's components and the check flags hard-coded and undefined tokens. When a design system was already saved from the same app, it reports what changed since. Bounded to 2,000 files and 1 MB; never reads .env files.

root.description: Workspace-relative folder of the app, for a monorepo (default the workspace root).

name.description: A name for the design system to save from the app, e.g. "Acme app". Only after the user agrees to save one.

tools.name: read_open_design_source
tools.description: Converts a workspace document (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, PDF, Markdown, text or CSV) into Markdown under the output directory's sources/ folder, extracts its embedded images, and returns an outline (headings with line ranges and sizes), never the full text. Read the returned markdownPath yourself, by line range, for the sections you need. Cached by content hash. Use it to look into a source before deciding how to use it; prepare_open_design_brief with `sources` calls it for you. PDFs need `pdftotext` (poppler); without it the result says to read the PDF with your own tools.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the document, e.g. "docs/q3-report.docx" or "CHANGELOG.md".

tools.name: prepare_open_design_brief
tools.description: Composes generation instructions for an Open Design artifact by combining the chosen skill's workflow, an optional design system's visual tokens, universal craft rules, and the user's brief. Returns an 'instructions' string you must follow, plus a 'suggestedEntryPath'. Does NOT write any files — after calling it, author the entry file (and any supporting files) yourself with your normal file-editing tools, then call register_open_design_artifact.

skillId.description: A skill id from list_open_design_skills, in its full 'od:<mode>:<name>' form.

designSystemId.description: Optional design system id from list_open_design_design_systems. If omitted, falls back to the active design system. If given explicitly, it also becomes the new active one.

brief.description: The user's design brief / request, in their own words.

collectionId.description: Set this (a slug you derive once from the collection name, reused verbatim on every call) when this artifact is one screen of a multi-screen design collection — see the "design collections" guidance for the full workflow.

collectionName.description: A short display name for the collection, e.g. "Fintech Onboarding Flow". Required together with collectionId.

screenRole.description: Required together with collectionId â this screen's short role label, e.g. "splash", "value-prop", "checkout".

redesign.description: For a redesign of a live website: { site, owned }. Reads the content inventory that extract_open_design_design_system wrote with content: true (call that first) and the audit_open_design_site findings if the site was audited, and adds a section binding the site's own words, listing the problems to fix and, unless owned is true, the concept ribbon. Use the open-design-redesign skill.

site.description: The site being redesigned, as given to extraction.

owned.description: True only when the user says the site is theirs or the work is commissioned: no concept ribbon.

baseScreen.description: For a redesign of a screen that exists: a workspace image (PNG, JPEG, WebP) of it, or its URL (e.g. the app's dev server page, captured in a browser). Stored under .open-design/.bases/ (never published); the instructions treat it as the screen to change, and the check shows it beside the new design.

screenTotal.description: Optional: the total number of screens you've planned for this collection, for an accurate "screen N of M" framing.

sources.description: Workspace paths of documents to build the design from (1–10): reports, specs, spreadsheets, existing decks, or repository files such as CHANGELOG.md or docs/adr/*.md. When given, the instructions add the extracted material, a storyline-first workflow (write outline.md, get the user's approval, then build) and accuracy rules.

format.description: Optional canvas format. Adds a Canvas section with the exact size, units, safe area and, for print, bleed and minimum type size, so any skill can produce a post or poster at that size. Screen: x-image (1600×900), ig-square (1080×1080 per card), ig-portrait (1080×1350), pinterest-pin (1000×1500, 20 MB), story (1080×1920), xhs-card (1080×1440 per card), yt-thumbnail (1280×720), linkedin-image (1200×627), og-image (1200×630), x-header (1500×500), linkedin-banner (1584×396), email-header (600×200, captured at 2×), and display ads banner-mrec (300×250), banner-leaderboard (728×90), banner-skyscraper (160×600), banner-mobile (320×50), and shop images shop-product (2048×2048), shop-banner (1920×800), shop-collection (1920×600). Print (trim sizes, authored in mm with bleed): a4, a3, a2, a1, a0, a5, a6, a7, letter, tabloid, poster-18x24, poster-24x36, postcard-4x6, business-card, business-card-us, and cards with rounded corners trading-card, tarot-card, mini-card. Pass the same id as format to register_open_design_artifact.

fluid.description: With format (or alone): build a fluid design that reflows to any canvas shape, sized in container units with layout rules for wide and tall shapes; the shape is then picked at export (preset/presets) or in the preview, without regenerating. Default: true for print formats, false for screen formats (social recipes need exact pixels). fluid: true without format uses A3 as the default shape. Use it for posters.

answers.description: Optional: the user's answers to the surface's (and the design-system recommender's) questions, by question id, e.g. { "where": "Printed" }. Written into the instructions as decisions to build to.

assumptions.description: Optional: what you decided without asking, up to six short lines, e.g. ["dark theme", "one sign-up button"]. Written into the instructions; list them to the user in one sentence when the design is ready.

tools.name: prepare_open_design_exploration
tools.description: Use INSTEAD of prepare_open_design_brief when the user explicitly asks for options, directions, alternatives or several versions of a design. Assigns 2–4 deliberately different directions (visual styles when no design system is active, layout/narrative structures when one is, or labels you pass for a named axis), writes the exploration's plan, and returns sharedInstructions plus one short instructions block, entry path and directionId per direction. Directions are quick sketches; only the one the user picks is built out. Writes no design files: write each direction yourself (follow sharedInstructions + that direction's instructions), register it with explorationId and directionId, then call compare_open_design_exploration. STYLE TILES: with skillId od:design-system:style-tile the directions are compact color + type tiles (default 4, visual axis even with an active design system; axis "custom" with an active system evolves it). Choosing one with next "save-design-system" copies the tile's tokens verbatim.

skillId.description: A skill id from list_open_design_skills, in its full 'od:<mode>:<name>' form.

brief.description: The user's design brief / request, in their own words.

count.description: How many directions: 2–4, default 3; for the style-tile skill 2–6, default 4.

axis.description: What the directions differ in. Omit for the default: 'structure' when a design system is active (brand stays fixed), otherwise 'visual'. 'visual' with an active design system sets that system aside for this exploration. 'custom' needs customDirections.

directionIds.description: Optional: pick specific directions instead of the default order. Visual ids: modern-minimal, human-approachable, tech-utility, editorial-monocle (editorial/publishing briefs), brutalist-experimental (art, agency, manifesto). Structure ids for pages: classic-hero-grid, story-led-scroll, product-ui-first, dense-utility; for decks: problem-solution, narrative-journey, data-led, demo-first.

customDirections.description: For a user-named axis (e.g. "three hero concepts"): 2–4 directions (style tiles: up to 6), each a distinct label and a one-paragraph brief.

designSystemId.description: Optional design system id. If omitted, the active one is used. If given, it also becomes the active one.

tools.name: compare_open_design_exploration
tools.description: Call after registering an exploration's directions. Refreshes and returns the path of its comparison page (compare.html: every direction side by side, opens in any browser from the file system), lists registered and missing directions, and with contactSheet: true renders a PNG of the comparison with the installed browser. If you can view images, check the contact sheet that the directions really differ before showing the user.

contactSheet.description: Also render the comparison page to exports/contact-sheet.png. Default false.

tools.name: choose_open_design_direction
tools.description: Call when the user picks a direction from an exploration. Records the choice (marked on the comparison page) and returns instructions for the next step: 'build-out' builds the chosen sketch out at full fidelity, 'merge' does the same while taking named aspects from other directions (needs mergeFrom), and 'save-design-system' turns the direction into a reusable custom design system. Writes no design files.

directionId.description: The chosen direction id. It must already be registered.

next.description: What to do with the chosen direction.

notes.description: Optional: the user's own adjustments, in their words.

aspect.description: What to take, e.g. "hero", "colour palette", "pricing table".

mergeFrom.description: Required for 'merge': which aspects to take from which other directions.

tools.name: register_open_design_artifact
tools.description: Call this AFTER you have written an artifact's entry file (and any supporting files) into the workspace with your normal file-editing tools. Validates the artifact and writes its manifest sidecar (<entry>.artifact.json) next to the entry file. Fails clearly if entryPath does not exist yet.

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the artifact's entry file.

title.description: A short human-readable title for the artifact.

supportingFiles.description: Workspace-relative paths to sibling files the entry depends on, relative to the entry file's directory.

sourceSkillId.description: The skillId used to generate this artifact, if any.

designSystemId.description: The designSystemId used to generate this artifact, if any.

collectionId.description: The same collectionId passed to prepare_open_design_brief, if this screen is part of a design collection.

collectionName.description: The same collectionName passed to prepare_open_design_brief, if this screen is part of a design collection.

screenIndex.description: 0-based position of this screen within its collection (0 for the first screen, 1 for the second, ...).

screenRole.description: The same screenRole passed to prepare_open_design_brief, if this screen is part of a design collection.

flow.description: The same flow plan passed to prepare_open_design_brief, for a screen of a planned flow. Stored as the manifest's metadata.flow with this screen's id (its screenRole).

explorationId.description: The explorationId from prepare_open_design_exploration, if this artifact belongs to a design exploration. Updates its comparison page.

directionId.description: The direction's directionId, for an exploration sketch. Leave it out for a built-out or merged version registered against the exploration.

sources.description: The same source document paths passed to prepare_open_design_brief. Records each source's hash in the manifest and, for HTML, reports numbers on the page that appear in none of the sources so you can check them.

format.description: The canvas format passed to prepare_open_design_brief (or the adaptation's registerArgs), if any. Recorded in the manifest's metadata.format so export, preflight and adaptation use it without repeating it.

resolvedCommentIds.description: Ids of the user's comments (from get_open_design_artifact's openComments) that this edit addressed. They're marked resolved and their pins leave the preview.

answers.description: The same answers passed to prepare_open_design_brief.

assumptions.description: The same assumptions passed to prepare_open_design_brief.

brief.description: What was asked and assumed for this design, stored as the manifest's metadata.brief (the latest replaces the earlier one) so later edits and checks can see it. Leave it out on an edit that changed none of it.

tools.name: get_open_design_artifact
tools.description: Reads back a registered Open Design artifact: its manifest, entry file content, supporting file list, and the user's unaddressed comments from the browser preview or VS Code ('openComments', status open or sent). Each comment names its element (selector, text excerpt, htmlHint, rect) and its note; up to 4 comment screenshots are attached as images, newest first, and every comment's screenshot path is listed. Call it when the user says they left comments; address each one, then pass their ids as resolvedCommentIds to register_open_design_artifact. With critique: true it instead returns what the design critic judges (the open-design-critique skill): the recorded brief, title and skill id, the design system's DESIGN.md, the latest saved check run's findings and screenshot paths, and the last critique, with that run's screenshots attached.

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the artifact's entry file.

critique.description: Return the critique input instead of the entry content and comments. Default false.

tools.name: open_open_design_preview
tools.description: Shows a registered Open Design artifact to the user in a live browser preview: an app window of their installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium (else their default browser; else it returns the URL to open). The preview reloads whenever the design's files change. In its Comment mode the user clicks an element to leave a comment with a screenshot; its Send to agent button copies an instruction for them to paste here, and get_open_design_artifact returns the comments. Its Checks panel shows the screenshots of each check_open_design_artifact run, before and after. Call it once per session after the first register_open_design_artifact, unless the user declined; later calls switch the same window to another artifact. Omit entryPath for a list of the workspace's designs. Pass open: false to only get the URL.

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered artifact's entry file. Omit for the list of designs.

open.description: Open a window (default true). false only starts the preview and returns its URL.

tools.name: set_up_open_design_browser_pane
tools.description: For Claude Desktop's Code tab only (where its preview tool, named like preview_start, is in your tools): adds the open-design-preview configuration to this workspace's .claude/launch.json (created if missing; other configurations are kept; only its own entry is replaced), so the Code tab can run the live browser preview in its Browser pane. Returns the configuration name and port. Then start that configuration with the Code tab's preview tool; the pane opens on the newest registered design. Call it once per project, before the first time you show a design in the Code tab, and tell the user once that you added a preview entry to .claude/launch.json. Elsewhere use open_open_design_preview.

tools.name: show_open_design_artifact
tools.description: Shows a registered Open Design artifact, or an exploration's directions side by side, or a fluid master's campaign sheet, to the user inline in the conversation, in hosts that render MCP Apps (Claude Desktop Chat). There the user can switch to Comment mode, click an element and leave a comment, then click "Ask Claude to apply", which posts a message here naming the comment ids; export buttons post a request for export_open_design_artifact (the page never downloads). For an exploration, "Take this one" posts the user's pick; confirm the next step with them before calling choose_open_design_direction. A style-tile exploration also offers "Use as design system", which asks directly for next: "save-design-system". With campaign: true (after export_open_design_artifact with campaignSheet: true) it shows every tile of the master's campaign sheet with its errors; "Fix this piece" posts the tile and its errors here. Every host also gets a text result (title, path, open comments, or the campaign tiles); hosts without MCP Apps are told to use open_open_design_preview. In Claude Desktop Chat call it after the first register_open_design_artifact of a design: the copy shown then follows later edits and comments by itself, so call it again only for another design or when the user asks to see it again. Pass entryPath, or explorationId for an exploration.

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered artifact's entry file.

explorationId.description: An exploration id from prepare_open_design_exploration, to show its directions instead.

campaign.description: With a fluid master's entryPath: show its last campaign sheet, tile by tile, instead of the design.

return_literals: Viewer link (opens in any browser, read-only, kept while the project is): {link}

tools.name: show_open_design_examples
tools.description: Shows the remixable Open Design examples to the user inline as a gallery of live previews, in hosts that render MCP Apps (Claude Desktop Chat), so they can pick a starting point by eye. "Remix this" posts a message here naming the example's skillId; then call remix_open_design_example with it (ask what to make first if the user hasn't said). The page copies nothing itself. Filter with query, mode or surface (a surface id, as list_open_design_skills takes). Only listed to hosts that render MCP Apps; elsewhere use list_open_design_skills with remixableOnly: true.

query.description: Free-text filter, matched against name, description and triggers.

surface.description: A surface id (prototype, slides, poster, â¦): only that surface's examples.

tools.name: show_open_design_design_systems
tools.description: Shows Open Design design systems to the user inline as tiles (palette swatches, fonts, active mark), in hosts that render MCP Apps (Claude Desktop Chat); opening a tile shows its Visualize page. "Use this design system" posts a message here naming the id; then call set_active_design_system with it. Pass ids for a shortlist (shown in that order), or query and category to filter. Only listed to hosts that render MCP Apps; elsewhere use list_open_design_design_systems.

query.description: Free-text filter on id, name, summary and category.

ids.description: A shortlist of design system ids; query and category are ignored.

tools.name: show_open_design_questions
tools.description: Asks the user up to four short questions inline as tappable choices, in hosts that render MCP Apps (Claude Desktop Chat), instead of a wall of chat text: surface and design-system questions before a build, a direction pick after an exploration, a "fix these?" question after a review. Each question has an id, text and kind (single, multi or text); single and multi take up to eight options (id, label, and optionally imageRef: designSystem:<id>, example:<skillId>, artifact:<entryPath> or checkRun:<entryPath>[#<runId>], never a URL). The view adds a "You pick" choice. Send posts one message here starting "Answers:" with a line <!-- od-answers {...} -->: read that JSON (question id to option id, option ids, typed text, or "you-pick", meaning choose for them). Don't repeat the questions in chat; accept typed answers too. Only listed to hosts that render MCP Apps; if called elsewhere it returns the questions as a numbered list to ask in one message.

title.description: A short heading, e.g. "A few quick questions".

id.description: A short key for the answer, e.g. "where".

kind.description: single (default): one choice; multi: any number; text: a short typed answer.

default.description: A preselected option id (single), option ids (multi) or text.

tools.name: get_open_design_preview_state
tools.description: Used by the Open Design preview page only: a view's data (the design with its comments and check screenshots, an exploration, a page of examples, design-system tiles, a campaign sheet), one example's or design system's preview, or a question option's picture (imageRef).

revisionOnly.description: Only the shown design's revision, to tell whether it changed.

tools.name: save_open_design_comment
tools.description: Used by the Open Design preview page only: creates or edits one comment (merged by id) or deletes one, in the artifact's comments sidecar.

comment.description: The whole comment record to create or edit.

deleteId.description: The id of a comment to delete.

tools.name: set_active_design_system
tools.description: Sets (or clears, if designSystemId is omitted/empty) the active Open Design design system, persisted for this workspace. Used automatically by prepare_open_design_brief whenever called without an explicit designSystemId.

designSystemId.description: A design system id from list_open_design_design_systems. Omit or pass an empty string to clear.

writeProjectDesignMd.description: Also write the design system as DESIGN.md at the project root, for tools such as Impeccable that read one. Only when the user agrees. Never overwrites: if the project already has a DESIGN.md (root, .agents/context/ or docs/), it is kept unchanged.

tools.name: create_open_design_design_system
tools.description: Composes instructions for authoring a brand-new, custom design system as a DESIGN.md file plus a sibling tokens.css following the Open Design token contract. Writes no DESIGN.md or tokens.css; with kind it writes the system's brand.json (own brand or reference, descriptor, and from evidenceDir the source URLs and the site screenshot as reference.png), which the recommender, the check and the critic read. If sourceUrl is given, performs a best-effort extraction of candidate colors/fonts from that page. After writing the files, call set_active_design_system with the returned id. To write ONLY a tokens.css for an existing custom design system (id starting with user:), pass existingDesignSystemId instead of name/brief.

name.description: A short name for the design system. Required unless existingDesignSystemId is given.

brief.description: A description of the brand, in the user's own words. Required unless existingDesignSystemId is given.

sourceUrl.description: Optional: a website URL to take a rough starting palette and fonts from, by reading its source. For a design system that matches a site, call extract_open_design_design_system first instead: it renders the page and measures it.

existingDesignSystemId.description: Optional: the id of an existing custom design system (user:…). Returns instructions to write only its tokens.css, from its current DESIGN.md.

kind.description: Optional: own when this is the user's own brand (DESIGN.md is headed '<Name> Design System', the recommender puts it first, and the check and critic hold designs to it); reference for a look taken from someone else's site ('Design System Inspired by <Name>'). Writes brand.json.

descriptor.description: Optional, with kind: what the recommender matches on, as for bundled systems.

moods.description: e.g. calm, playful, premium, technical, bold, minimal, warm, romantic

industries.description: e.g. fintech, saas, retail, food, health, education, dating

evidenceDir.description: Optional, with kind: the bundleDir extract_open_design_design_system returned. Records the source URLs, keeps the site screenshot as reference.png, writes review.html, and puts the brand kit into brand.json: marks (copied into assets/ for an own brand only), fonts with their source, component specs, voice facts (and, for an own brand, the sampled lines) and imagery.

fontLicence.description: Optional, with kind own and evidenceDir: 'confirmed' when the user says they hold the licence for the brand's self-hosted fonts. Only then are the font files the site loaded copied into the design system's assets/fonts/. Never for a reference site.

tools.name: audit_open_design_site
tools.description: Audits a live website with Open Design's own checks, for a redesign pitch or an owner's own site. Renders each page in an installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium at desktop (1440×900) and phone (390×844) sizes and reports what a visitor runs into: text contrast, tap targets, sideways scrolling, 320 px reflow, layout with larger text, overflowing or covered text, the first phone screen with nothing to tap, broken images, styles or scripts, images without alt text, a missing viewport tag, download size and request count, and default-template looks. Checks that need Open Design markup (states, flows, sample data, tokens) don't run. Writes <output folder>/.audits/<site>/: audit.json with every finding, screenshots, crops of the top problems and index.html, a short plain-language report with the 5 biggest problems ranked by what they cost a visitor and a statement of what wasn't measured. Gives no score and makes no speed or SEO claims. Only public http(s) pages; at most 4 pages on one site, 20 seconds each; no logins, cookies or form submissions. A bot check, login wall or empty page comes back as blocked with its screenshot.

url.description: The page to audit, usually the home page.

extraUrls.description: Optional: up to 3 more pages on the same site (menu, services, contact) to audit too.

tools.name: compare_open_design_before_after
tools.description: For a redesign with a base screen (the page as it was): writes a before/after page beside the design (one section per page of a collection) with the old and new pages at desktop (1440×900) and phone (390×844) sizes, a drag slider and side-by-side view, and capture times. When the site was audited (audit_open_design_site), each audit problem for that page is re-checked on the design with the same check at the same size and shown as fixed only if it passes, otherwise as still open (page weight isn't re-checked). Lists every copy edit (data-od-copy-edit) with its original. Optional summary lines must each cite fixed findings by id; a line that cites nothing or an open finding is left out and reported. The page is one self-contained HTML file, registered as its own design, so preview, PDF export (one page per screen) and publish work on it; a flow's published site links to it from the map. Needs a browser to capture the design.

entryPath.description: One redesigned page. Give this or collectionId.

collectionId.description: Every page of a redesign planned as a flow. Give this or entryPath.

text.description: One short line for the client (at most 160 characters), e.g. "The booking button is now readable and on the first phone screen."

cites.description: The ids of the fixed findings the line rests on, e.g. ["F1", "F3"].

summary.description: Optional: up to 3 summary lines for the top of the page. Run once without it to see which findings are fixed, then again with lines that cite them.

tools.name: save_open_design_project
tools.description: Saves to the designer's work library (portfolio/ in the designs folder), which every portfolio output reads: the owner (name, role, location, bio, email, links), the library's style (a design system id), the project order, one project's facts, and edits to its imported assets (alt text, captions, privacy, redaction boxes, device). A new project needs a title, the designer's role and a privacy level: public, unlisted (only for people the designer sends it to) or internal (under NDA or only for a promotion packet). Every outcome needs a source: measured (the designer has the number), estimated (shown with "about") or qualitative (no number). Never invent facts: ask the designer for what's missing; the reply lists it. Fields you pass replace the stored ones; fields you leave out stay. An asset can't be looser than its project. Changing redactions remakes the asset's copies in a browser so no output can show what a box covers.

owner.description: The designer: { name, role, location, bio, email, links: [{ label, url }] }. Only what they gave you.

style.description: A design system id from list_open_design_design_systems to use as the portfolio's look, or "" to clear it.

order.description: Project slugs in the order the designer wants them shown.

project.description: One project's facts. slug picks an existing project; a new one is named from its title. Fields: title, role, privacy, company, client, team, dates { start, end } (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD; end may be "now"), platforms, problem, constraints, decisions [{ choice, rejected, why, tradeOff }], outcomes [{ text, value, source }], links [{ kind: live | prototype | write-up | other, url, label }], tags, designs (entry paths of kit designs made for it).

assets.description: Edits to the project's imported assets (pass project: { slug } with them): { id, alt, confirmAlt, caption, privacy (or null for the project's), redactions [{ x, y, width, height }] from 0 to 1 ([] clears), device, assetKind, remove }. Alt text you write stays a draft until the designer confirms it (confirmAlt: true).

tools.name: get_open_design_library
tools.description: Reads the designer's work library: the owner, the portfolio style, and each project in order with its privacy level, asset count and what it still lacks for a case study. With project, returns that project's facts and assets in full (ids, sizes, privacy, alt text and whether it is a draft, redaction boxes). Read it before any portfolio work, and use only facts it holds.

project.description: A project slug, for its full facts and assets.

tools.name: import_open_design_work
tools.description: Brings the designer's own work into a work library project (save the project first). Sources: { kind: "file", path } an image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) or MP4 in the workspace; { kind: "data", data, name } an image as base64 (for files the person attached); { kind: "url", url } a live page captured at desktop (1440 wide) and phone (390 wide), first screen or fullPage; { kind: "design", entryPath } a kit design captured the same way; { kind: "figma", url } a Figma frame as a picture, through the Figma token, or with data from the Figma connector's get_screenshot (the reply says how). Each source may carry alt (your draft, which stays a draft until the designer confirms it), caption, assetKind, device and privacy. Every image loses its camera and location metadata, keeps one original and gets WebP copies 800, 1400 and 2800 px wide (needs a browser). Images under 1600 px wide are flagged. Returns a small copy of each image so you can draft its alt text. At most 20 sources, 25 MB per image, 100 MB per video.

data.description: kind data or figma: the image as base64.

name.description: A short name for the asset id, e.g. "checkout-before".

url.description: kind url: the live page; kind figma: the frame link with node-id.

entryPath.description: kind design: the design's entry file.

fullPage.description: kind url or design: capture the whole page, not only the first screen.

device.description: The device a screen is for, so share images can frame it.

privacy.description: Stricter than the project's, if this one image is more private.

tools.name: extract_open_design_design_system
tools.description: Renders a website in an installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium (consent banners and chat launchers hidden, never clicked; each page scrolled once) and measures its design system: colour roles from the elements that carry them (page background, cards, text tiers, borders, the primary button and its forced :hover/:active/:focus-visible states, status colours from alerts and invalid fields), declared CSS custom properties, the fonts it loaded, text sizes, radii, spacing, container width and motion. Writes an evidence bundle (evidence.json, screenshots, one crop per role, the logo) under <output folder>/.extract/<site>/ and returns a draft token set on the Open Design token contract, with where each value came from and which tokens nothing measured. Does NOT write DESIGN.md or tokens.css: write both from the draft, keeping measured values as measured (the open-design-design-system-from-url skill has the steps), then save it as a custom design system. Only public http(s) pages; at most 4 pages, 20 seconds each; no logins, cookies or form submissions. A bot check, login wall or empty page comes back as blocked with its screenshot. With no browser installed, falls back to reading the page source and stylesheets and marks the result partial. Also takes sources instead of, or as well as, a url: a screenshot, pasted CSS (custom properties, Tailwind theme or design-tokens JSON), page source, a brand guide document or a PowerPoint template (.pptx, .potx). Each value then carries a confidence (measured, declared, stated, sampled); where sources disagree the more confident value wins and the other is listed under conflicts. A Figma file or frame link in url is not fetched: the tool returns the steps to read the file with the Figma connector and call back with the replies as a figma source. A Canva design link in url is not fetched either: the tool returns the steps to export the design with the Canva connector (PPTX plus up to 4 PNG pages) and call back with the export links as template and screenshot sources (fileUrl); Canva's connector can't read a Brand Kit's values.

url.description: The page to measure, e.g. the home page; or a Figma file or frame link (the tool then returns what to read with the Figma connector). Optional when sources are given.

extraUrls.description: Optional: up to 3 more pages on the same site (a product or pricing page) to fill in roles the first page lacks.

theme.description: Which theme to measure (default light). dark and both measure a dark theme only if the site has one (prefers-color-scheme or a theme attribute on the root element).

content.description: For a redesign: also copy each page's content verbatim (headings, copy, calls to action, navigation, contact details, opening hours, prices, images with alt text) into content.json in the same visit. Pages robots.txt disallows are skipped and reported as blocked.

localizeImages.description: With content: copy the images the pages loaded into the bundle. Only when the user says the site is theirs or the client has commissioned the work; otherwise images stay as the site's URLs.

discover.description: With no extraUrls: also measure up to 3 pages linked from the home page's header and footer navigation (pricing, product or features, about, docs or blog first; never sign-in, sign-up, legal or careers pages, or pages robots.txt disallows), so tokens are elected by how many pages use them. Default true; false measures only url.

sources.description: Optional: up to 6 other sources to draft from, with or without a url. A blocked site, a site behind a login, or a brand with no site: ask for a screenshot, the CSS, a brand guide or a PowerPoint template. Screenshots give sampled colours only (fonts need confirming); templates and brand guides give declared values. A figma source is the replies the agent read from a Figma file through Figma's connector: pass the file link, each token frame's get_variable_defs map, and the search_design_system items. A Canva design comes in as its exports: a template and screenshots given by fileUrl (Canva export links only), each with canva: { design, pages }.

kind.description: screenshot: a PNG of the site or app. css: a stylesheet, a Tailwind theme or W3C design-tokens JSON. html: page source. brandGuide: a PDF, DOCX, PPTX or Markdown guide with colour codes and fonts. template: a PowerPoint template (.pptx or .potx). figma: a Figma file the agent read with Figma's connector (see file, frames and designSystem).

text.description: For css and html: the text itself (at most 2 MB).

data.description: For a screenshot or template: the file as base64 (screenshot at most 4 MB, template 20 MB).

fileUrl.description: For a screenshot or template exported from Canva: export-design's download link, as Canva returned it. Downloaded only from Canva's export host (export-download.canva.com), at most 20 MB; any other host is refused.

canva.description: For a screenshot or template exported from Canva: which design (its link) and, for a screenshot, which page numbers. Turns on reading fonts from the slides.

name.description: Optional: a label for the source in the draft (e.g. "brand guide 2024").

file.description: For figma: the Figma file link (or its key).

frames.description: For figma: each token frame and the primary button, with the get_variable_defs reply for that frame.

name.description: The frame's name; it says which role the frame plays.

link.description: The frame's link, for the record.

variables.description: The get_variable_defs reply: a resolved name-to-value map.

fill.description: For the primary button: its fill colour, when read directly.

text.description: For the primary button: the colour of the text on it.

designSystem.description: For figma: the search_design_system items: each variable's name, collection, scopes and description.

scopes.description: Figma scopes, e.g. FRAME_FILL, TEXT_FILL, STROKE_COLOR, CORNER_RADIUS.

styles.description: For figma: read the file's published styles through Figma's REST API with this machine's token (local server only). Use when Figma is not connected.

modes.description: For figma: the collections and modes the design-system search named.

read.description: The mode the frames show, when it is known.

logos.description: For figma: the logo frames you exported, one entry per role. The local server saves the files into the bundle; the hosted server lists them as needed, so pass role and name only there.

role.description: Where the logo belongs in the design system.

name.description: The file name to save it as, e.g. "acme-logo.svg".

data.description: The exported file as base64 (at most 1 MB). Local server only.

path.description: A workspace-relative file you already wrote. Local server only.

seenOn.description: The background colour it was seen on, #rrggbb.

fonts.description: For figma: each font family the file names, with its weights. Figma holds no font files, so they are listed as needed.

compareTo.description: To refresh a saved design system (user:…): measure the site again (from the URLs its brand.json recorded when url is left out) and return, under refresh, the tokens, fonts, component specs and marks added, changed or removed. Changes nothing in the design system.

tools.name: export_open_design_design_system
tools.description: Writes a design system in Claude Design's Design System format (project/design-system.json, project/tokens.json, project/README.md) into <output folder>/claude-design/<id>/, checked against that format, plus a brand.html page (the showcase, marks, voice, do and don't) registered as an artifact. For the user's own brand it also copies the logo, icons and licensed font files to project/assets/ and adds a fonts note; a reference system gets no marks. Writes files only: publish them with your Artifact tool to make a Claude Design System artifact. Works for bundled and custom systems.

designSystemId.description: The design system to export, e.g. user:acme. Default: the active one.

by.description: Optional: who the export is recorded for in Claude's lastChange.

tools.name: port_open_design_artifact_to_app
tools.description: Composes instructions for porting a finished Open Design artifact's design into this workspace's actual, existing application as real, idiomatic production code. Does NOT write any files. Directs the model to ground the port in a real existing component and explicitly excludes routing/navigation wiring.

entryPath.description: The workspace-relative path of the artifact to promote.

targetComponentPath.description: Optional: where the new component/code file should be written.

referenceComponentPath.description: Optional: an existing component file to use as the pattern reference.

tools.name: prepare_open_design_component_library
tools.description: Composes staged instructions for turning reviewed Open Design artifacts into a reusable component set on a named React library: Material UI themed to Material 3 (`mui`), shadcn/ui (`shadcn`), or React Native components styled with NativeWind for Expo apps (`nativewind`). Use it when the user asks for components, a component library or a component set from a design ("make Material 3 components for my React app from this"); for putting one page into the app, use port_open_design_artifact_to_app instead. Returns a repeated-element inventory to turn into components.md (then stop for the user's approval), a ready theme generated from the design system's tokens, component and gallery rules, and how to record the set. Does NOT write app code. Call it again with `record` after the set builds: that writes metadata.componentLibrary on the artifacts' manifests so a later run updates the same set.

entryPaths.description: Workspace-relative entry paths of 1 to 10 registered artifacts the set is built from.

collectionId.description: Instead of entryPaths: every screen of this collection.

library.description: "mui" (Material UI, themed to Material 3), "shadcn" (shadcn/ui), "nativewind" (React Native components styled with NativeWind, for Expo and React Native apps), or "auto" (default) to pick from the app's package.json (an Expo or React Native app always gets "nativewind").

outputDir.description: Optional: workspace-relative folder for the components, inside the app. Default: <app>/src/components/<DesignName>, or the folder an earlier record names.

record.description: Stage 5 only: the finished set, written to the artifacts' manifests instead of returning instructions.

tools.name: pull_open_design_figma_frame
tools.description: Composes instructions for translating a Figma frame into a real code artifact with 1:1 visual fidelity. When the user's Figma MCP server is connected (checked via list_open_design_integrations), the instructions use Figma's own get_design_context, get_variable_defs and get_screenshot; no token needed. A Figma personal access token is optional: when one is configured, the frame's structural summary and a rendered image are fetched too and included as ground truth, and it's the fallback when Figma isn't connected. Does NOT write any files — author the entry file yourself with your normal file-editing tools, then call register_open_design_artifact. figmaUrl must be a frame-scoped link (Figma's "Copy link to selection", with node-id), not a bare file link.

figmaUrl.description: A Figma frame URL, e.g. from "Copy link to selection" — must include a node-id.

designSystemId.description: Optional design system id from list_open_design_design_systems to align the translated code with.

tools.name: remix_open_design_example
tools.description: Copies a curated Open Design example artifact (identified by its skillId, which must have remixable: true) into the workspace as a starting point, registers it, and returns instructions to MODIFY the copied file rather than regenerate it from scratch.

tools.name: export_open_design_artifact
tools.description: Renders a registered Open Design artifact in a headless browser (an installed Chrome, Edge, or Chromium) and writes upload-ready file(s) under the artifact's own exports/ folder. Does not modify the artifact's source files. IMAGES (png/jpeg): use after register_open_design_artifact whenever the user wants an image to post (X, Instagram, Xiaohongshu, a YouTube thumbnail, a poster). Size comes from explicit width/height, else the source skill's aspect hint, else each selected element's box, else 1080×1080. For multi-card designs mark each card with data-od-card and pass selector "[data-od-card]" for one numbered image per card. Pass maxBytes with the platform's upload limit (X 5000000, YouTube thumbnail 2000000, Instagram 8000000) and images are re-encoded as JPEG until they fit. DECKS: format "pptx" gives a PowerPoint file with one full-bleed slide image per slide (pixel-perfect, not editable text); add editable: true for an editable PowerPoint instead (<name>-editable.pptx: real text boxes, shapes and pictures placed from the browser's layout, with gradients, SVG diagrams and effects on a background picture per slide; close to the deck, not identical; the result lists what stayed a picture and which web fonts PowerPoint will need). When a user wants slides to edit in PowerPoint, Keynote or Google Slides, use editable: true; never write your own conversion script. format "pdf" gives one page per slide. Slides are captured at the deck's own measured slide size, at scale 2 by default. Artifacts registered with kind "deck" (or made from an od:deck:* skill) are detected automatically; pass deck: true if a deck was registered as "html". Pass slides (1-based numbers) with format png/jpeg to export just those slides as images. PAGES: format "pdf" on an ordinary page prints it with the browser's print engine (vector, selectable text, A4 unless the page's CSS sets a size). Not for video — HyperFrames videos are rendered with the HyperFrames CLI per the brief's instructions. POSTERS AND PREFLIGHT: page exports run preflight checks (text overflow, safe area, print bleed size, minimum type size, contrast, emoji, image resolution for print, QR codes that don't decode, broken assets) and list findings, errors first; findings never block the export. Pass checkOnly: true to check without writing files, and fix every error before the real export. Pass preset with a format id ("ig-portrait", "story", "a3"…) rather than width/height/selector/maxBytes. Pass data with a spreadsheet to export one poster, card or certificate per row. FLUID POSTERS (cards with data-od-fluid): preset reflows the design to that shape in the rendered page (the file is unchanged); presets exports several shapes at once; shapeSheet shows them all in one image. EMAIL AND PASTE: format "email" writes an inbox-safe email (and checks for what breaks in Gmail and Outlook: flex/grid layout, SVG, transforms, local images, missing alt, width over 640px, size over 102 KB); format "paste" with target wechat|notion|newsletter|generic writes an inlined fragment. Both compute styles in the browser, so Tailwind or any runtime CSS is inlined. To use the result, the user opens the file in a browser, selects all, copies and pastes. VIDEO AND GIF: format "mp4", "webm" or "gif" renders animated HTML (CSS animations, requestAnimationFrame, timers, data-duration storyboards, WebGL) frame by frame and encodes it with an installed ffmpeg (never downloaded; a 'no-ffmpeg' or 'ffmpeg-missing-encoder' error says what to install). Up to 60 seconds. Use maxBytes for platform limits (re-encodes smaller). HyperFrames compositions still render with the HyperFrames CLI.

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered artifact's entry file. Leave it out when collectionId is given.

collectionId.description: Export a whole collection as one clickable prototype: a single self-contained HTML file (assets inlined, shared navigation included) where the screens' links switch screens, written to <collection>/exports/<collectionId>-prototype.html. Other options are ignored.

format.description: Output format. png/jpeg: images; pdf: deck slides or a printed page; pptx: decks only; standalone: one self-contained .html with local CSS, scripts, images and fonts inlined (to attach or send); site: a deploy-ready folder (exports/site/) with index.html and its files (to publish â prefer publish_open_design_artifact, which builds it for you). standalone/site need no browser. Default png. email: an inbox-ready HTML email (exports/<name>.email.html, styles inlined, 600px column, preheader, dark-mode meta) plus a plain-text exports/<name>.email.txt, with email preflight; pass baseUrl once the artifact's assets are hosted so image URLs become absolute. paste: an inlined HTML fragment to paste into another editor (exports/<name>.<target>.html); needs target. mp4, webm, gif: animate the page on a virtual clock (frame-exact, the same on every run) and encode it with an installed ffmpeg; size from width/height, preset or the skill, duration from the page unless you pass duration.

width.description: Width in CSS pixels, given with height. Overrides the skill's size for images, the measured slide size for decks, or the print page size for page PDFs.

height.description: Viewport height in CSS pixels. Give together with width.

scale.description: Device scale factor (1–3). Default 2 for deck pptx/pdf (crisp when projected), 1 otherwise.

selector.description: CSS selector; each matching element is exported as its own numbered image (e.g. "[data-od-card]").

maxBytes.description: Per-file byte budget; over-budget images are re-encoded as progressively lower-quality JPEG until they fit.

deck.description: Force deck handling (true) or page handling (false). Omit to detect it from the artifact's kind and source skill.

slides.description: Decks only: 1-based slide numbers to export, e.g. [1, 3]. With png/jpeg, one image per slide; with pdf/pptx, only these slides in this order.

editable.description: Decks with format "pptx" only: an editable PowerPoint (native text boxes, shapes and pictures, written as <name>-editable.pptx) instead of one picture per slide. Default false.

badge.description: standalone/site only: add a small, closeable "Made with Open Design" footer badge. Default: on for site, off for standalone (OPEN_DESIGN_SHARE_BADGE overrides the default).

target.description: format "paste" only: where it will be pasted. wechat: top-level blocks become <section>s for the WeChat Official Account editor. notion: layout wrappers flattened and code-block languages kept, as Notion turns pasted HTML into blocks. newsletter: email rules and checks applied to the fragment. generic: any rich-text editor.

baseUrl.description: site: the https address the bundle will be served from, so the link-preview image (og:image) can be an absolute URL. email and paste: where the artifact's files are hosted; relative image and link URLs are rewritten against it.

embedAssets.description: standalone only: download the remote assets the page declares (a 3d-scene spec's assets, or an application/od-assets+json block: HDRIs, textures, glTF models with their files) and embed them in the page, so it works where other sites are blocked (a Claude artifact) or offline. The result lists each embedded asset and the page size; above 16 MB the export fails, naming the largest. An asset that can't be downloaded is reported and left as its URL.

maxResolution.description: With embedAssets: the highest Poly Haven resolution to fetch for textures and HDRIs (1k, 2k or 4k; default 1k). Models keep the resolution the page uses.

preset.description: A canvas format id instead of hand-copied sizes. Screen formats (x-image (1600×900), ig-square (1080×1080 per card), ig-portrait (1080×1350), pinterest-pin (1000×1500, 20 MB), story (1080×1920), xhs-card (1080×1440 per card), yt-thumbnail (1280×720), linkedin-image (1200×627), og-image (1200×630), x-header (1500×500), linkedin-banner (1584×396), email-header (600×200, captured at 2×), and display ads banner-mrec (300×250), banner-leaderboard (728×90), banner-skyscraper (160×600), banner-mobile (320×50), and shop images shop-product (2048×2048), shop-banner (1920×800), shop-collection (1920×600)) fill in width/height, selector "[data-od-card]" and the platform's byte budget. Print formats (a4, a3, a2, a1, a0, a5, a6, a7, letter, tabloid, poster-18x24, poster-24x36, postcard-4x6, business-card, business-card-us, and cards with rounded corners trading-card, tarot-card, mini-card) produce a print-ready PDF the size of the bleed box, with TrimBox and BleedBox set. Explicit arguments still win. Without preset, the format the artifact was registered with is used.

bleed.description: Print PDFs only: bleed in mm on every side. Default: the format's (3 mm for ISO sizes, 3.175 mm for US sizes). The card must be authored at trim size plus this bleed.

cropMarks.description: Print PDFs only: add crop marks at the trim corners in a 10 mm slug around the page.

dpi.description: Print images only (PNG or JPEG of a print format): the resolution, 150–600 (default 300). The image is the bleed box at this dpi, and the dpi is written into the file. Can't be combined with scale; over 8192 px a side is refused, naming the largest dpi that fits.

printHouse.description: A print-house profile id from list_open_design_print_houses, e.g. "boardgamesmaker". Writes each card face at that printer's exact upload size and file type (bleed included, only bleed removed), with -front/-back names and one back per card when the printer asks for it. The design's format must be one the printer takes. Can't be combined with dpi, scale, width/height, presets or selector.

checkOnly.description: Run the page load and preflight checks only, writing no files and leaving the manifest alone. Use it to check and fix a design before exporting.

data.description: Workspace-relative CSV, XLSX or JSON-array file. For each row, [data-od-field="<column>"] elements are filled (text, or src on img, href on a) and [data-od-qr-field="<column>"] gets a QR code, in the rendered page only (the file isn't changed). Images: one file per row; PDFs: one multi-page file (or split). At most 200 rows; every field must have a column.

sheet.description: XLSX data only: the sheet to read (default: the first).

nameField.description: With data: the column whose value names each row's file (slugified, made unique), e.g. "name" gives poster-ada-lovelace.png. Default: row numbers.

split.description: With data and a PDF format: one PDF per row instead of one multi-page PDF.

presets.description: Fluid designs only: export several canvas shapes in one call, each reflowed and preflighted at its own shape and written as <name>-<format>.<ext> (PDF for print shapes, PNG for screen shapes unless format is given). Can't be combined with preset, width or height. With data: one file per row per shape.

shapeSheet.description: Fluid designs only: also write exports/<name>-shapes.png, one image showing the design at every shape in presets (default: all catalog formats), each labelled and marked when preflight found errors there. With checkOnly: true it is the only file written. Use it to show the user how a poster looks in every size.

fps.description: mp4/webm/gif only: frames per second. Default 30 (15 for GIF).

duration.description: mp4/webm/gif only: length in seconds. Default: the sum of the frames' data-duration, else the longest CSS/Web animation, else 6.

loop.description: gif only: loop forever. Default true.

transparent.description: png only: capture without the page background, so everything the design doesn't paint is transparent — for cut-outs such as a 3D product shot to place on slides or pages. The page (and a 3D scene's renderer) must have a transparent background; a warning says so when every pixel came out opaque. PNGs aren't re-encoded to fit maxBytes when transparent.

shell.description: Device screens (data-od-device on <body>): PNG and JPEG exports show the screen inside the kit's generic device frame (status bar, cutout, home indicator, or a desktop title bar) by default. false exports the bare screen at the device's content size, for app store screenshots or handoff.

campaignSheet.description: Fluid designs: also write exports/campaign-sheet.png — the master at every shape in presets (default: the usual poster and social shapes), plus the first screen of every other piece registered in the master's collection (landing page, email…), each labelled and marked when it has preflight errors. Use it to show the user a whole campaign at a glance. With checkOnly: true it is the only file written.

return_literals: Export job {outcome.jobId} is still running. Call get_open_design_export_status with project "{project.id}" and jobId "{outcome.jobId}" in about 20 seconds to get the download links. Tell the user it's on its way.

tools.name: add_open_design_diagram_runtime
tools.description: Adds the diagram runtime to a diagram's HTML entry file, or updates it in place: one inline <script data-od-runtime="diagram"> block, placed before </body>, that lays the diagram out in the browser. It places nodes on a grid by rank and lane, draws right-angle connectors through the gaps between them with arrowheads and labels, boxes groups, and lays out sequence diagrams. The same file then renders identically in the preview, in export, in check_open_design_artifact and in any browser. Call it after writing the diagram markup (the diagram skill's workflow says when); it works before or after register_open_design_artifact and changes nothing else in the file. Never write, copy or edit the runtime yourself.
